traits.notes: The seedling exhibits pinnately compound leaves with serrate margins and a rugose surface texture. Fine trichomes are present on the leaflets and stems.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaflets emerging from the same node along the rachis in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaflets are densely arranged along the rachis)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the structure is clearly a leaf composed of multiple leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (a terminal leaflet is clearly visible at the apex of the leaf structure)
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 9 (counting the leaflets on the central leaf structure in the first image: four pairs plus one terminal leaflet)
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs at each node along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): toothed, serrate (distinct fine teeth are visible along the leaflet margins, especially in images 1 and 4)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate to elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval-shaped, widest below the middle)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaflets taper to a distinct, elongated point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears generally rounded)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent, well-spaced (the secondary veins are clearly visible, arching towards the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, rugose (the leaf surface is glossy and has a textured, wrinkled appearance due to the sunken veins)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible on the leaflets and petioles, particularly in image 5)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): long (the petiole and rachis are significantly longer than the individual leaflets)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petiole and rachis appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears soft, green, and non-woody)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the stem, especially in image 5)
    19.	Stem color: green (the stem is uniformly green)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively smooth, though with fine hairs)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no clear stipules are visible at the leaf base in any image)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct swollen joint is visible at the base of the petiole)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits pinnately compound leaves with serrate margins and a rugose surface texture. Fine trichomes are present on the leaflets and stems.
